text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Saturday, a working day this time for Latvia, prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament passed amendments to the land tax law, setting the land tax at 1.5 percent of the cadastral value of land.

- Pensions in Latvia will be increased by 11 lats next year, bringing the average pension to 51 lats at the end of 1997 against 40 lats in December 1996, the State Pensions Fund announced. Additional 35 million lats of the the state social budget will cover the increase.
- Latvian Citizenship and Immigration Board opened a new centre for printing passports to Latvia's non-citizens. The centre will be capable of issuing 1600 passports every day.
- Parliament passed amendments to a number of laws, including the laws on education, state pensions, mandatory social insurance, necessary to secure the fulfilment of the state budget of 1997.
- Speaker of the Russian State Duma Guennady Selezniyov has invited the Latvian Parliament Speaker Alfred Chepanis to visit the Russian Parliament early next year.
- Latvian and Estonian railways have agreed to close the line connecting the Latvian towns of Rujiena and Aloja.

- The international director of the Union of the Jewish human rights organisations in the US, Leonid Stonov, is currently on a fact finding visit to Latvia. He met both Speaker of the Latvian parliament Alfred Chepanis and Prime Minister Andris Shkele.

- 1996 may be called the year of stabilisation in the Latvian agriculture, with a successful privatisation of food processing plants, improvements in the field of payments and adoption of the law on agriculture.
